objects.description: Opaque handle representing a connection to the lldpd daemon. Allocated via lldpctl_new()/lldpctl_new_name() and freed with lldpctl_release(). Not thread-safe to share across threads concurrently. All I/O to/from the daemon is funneled through this connection using provided callbacks or built-in synchronous handlers.

Opaque reference-counted container for LLDP information (chassis, ports, VLANs, etc.). Use lldpctl_atom_get*/set* to query/modify fields, lldpctl_atom_iter* to iterate lists, and lldpctl_atom_inc_ref/lldpctl_atom_dec_ref for ownership. Some atoms require I/O to materialize via special getters (e.g., lldpctl_get_port).

Opaque iterator object used to iterate over iterable atoms (lists of ports, VLANs, etc.). Obtained from lldpctl_atom_iter() and advanced with lldpctl_atom_iter_next(); dereference to current element with lldpctl_atom_iter_value().

Const mapping entries from integer values to strings, used to translate discrete key values to human-readable names and back. Retrieved via lldpctl_key_get_map(). The array is terminated by an entry with value 0.

objects.description: Enumeration of library error codes returned by APIs or via lldpctl_last_error(). Use lldpctl_strerror() to get a descriptive string. Values are non-zero negatives for errors; 0 means no current error.
Enumeration for neighbor change notifications indicating deleted, updated, or added events delivered to watch callbacks.

objects.description: Enumeration of all retrievable/settable keys for atoms. Each enumerator’s comment documents how it can be accessed (A/S/B/I/L), writability, and semantics. Used with lldpctl_atom_get*/set* and iteration APIs.

functions.name: lldpctl_get_default_transport
functions.description: Return the default transport name/path used to contact the lldpd daemon (currently the default Unix socket location). Useful to discover where to connect when creating a connection.
requirements: None beyond calling it at any time; returns a statically managed C string.

functions.name: lldpctl_recv
functions.signature: ssize_t lldpctl_recv(lldpctl_conn_t *conn, const uint8_t *data, size_t length)
functions.description: Feed bytes received from lldpd into the library (typically for asynchronous IO). Processes notifications and pending replies. Returns the number of bytes consumed/available or a negative error on failure; 0 usually means a notification was processed.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection created by lldpctl_new()/lldpctl_new_name().
data must point to bytes received from lldpd; length is the number of bytes provided.
Caller must handle negative returns (library-specific errors such as LLDPCTL_ERR_*).
0 return is not an error and typically indicates a processed notification.

functions.name: lldpctl_send
functions.description: Notify the library that there is an opportunity to send pending bytes to lldpd (typically for asynchronous IO). The library will attempt to serialize and flush any queued messages via the user-provided send callback.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection created by lldpctl_new()/lldpctl_new_name().
Caller must handle negative returns (LLDPCTL_ERR_*).

functions.name: lldpctl_process_conn_buffer
functions.description: Check if additional notifications or data already buffered in the connection can be processed without new I/O. Intended for asynchronous connections.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection handle.
Return value 0 indicates maybe more data is available for processing; non-zero indicates no data or insufficient data.

functions.name: lldpctl_new
functions.description: Allocate a new lldpd connection handle using provided send/recv callbacks (asynchronous) or default synchronous Unix-socket callbacks if both are NULL. The handle encapsulates state and error information.
requirements: If both send and recv are NULL, the default synchronous I/O is used; otherwise both callbacks should implement the documented semantics and be prepared to return LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK/LLDPCTL_ERR_CALLBACK_FAILURE/LLDPCTL_ERR_EOF as applicable.
The returned handle must be released with lldpctl_release().
user_data is passed back to callbacks unchanged.

functions.name: lldpctl_new_name
functions.signature: lldpctl_conn_t *lldpctl_new_name(const char *ctlname, lldpctl_send_callback send, lldpctl_recv_callback recv, void *user_data)
functions.description: Allocate a new lldpd connection handle targeting the specified Unix-domain socket path. Uses provided callbacks for asynchronous I/O or defaults to synchronous I/O if both callbacks are NULL.
requirements: ctlname must point to the Unix-domain socket path for lldpd.
If both send and recv are NULL, the default synchronous I/O is used; otherwise callbacks must follow the documented return conventions.
The returned handle must be released with lldpctl_release().

functions.name: lldpctl_release
functions.description: Release resources associated with a connection handle allocated by lldpctl_new()/lldpctl_new_name().
requirements: conn must be a connection previously allocated by lldpctl_new()/lldpctl_new_name().
Return is 0 on success or a negative error code on failure; caller should handle negative error values.

functions.name: lldpctl_log_callback
functions.description: Register a custom developer-oriented logging callback to receive library log messages. When set, lldpctl_log_level() no longer has effect.
requirements: cb must be a valid function pointer expecting severity and a message C string.
Messages are for developers; applications should rely on return codes for user-facing errors.

functions.name: lldpctl_log_level
functions.description: Set the built-in log verbosity (1=warnings, 2=info, 3=debug). Has no effect if a log callback is registered via lldpctl_log_callback().
requirements: level should be one of 1, 2, or 3.
No effect if a custom log callback is registered.

functions.name: lldpctl_strerror
functions.description: Return a statically allocated human-readable description for an lldpctl_error_t error code.
requirements: error must be a value from lldpctl_error_t; the returned pointer is to a static string and must not be freed.

functions.name: lldpctl_last_error
functions.description: Get the last error associated with a connection. For functions that returned pointers, this provides the corresponding error code; for int-returning functions, it matches the negative error code.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection handle.
Returns 0 (LLDPCTL_NO_ERROR) if no error is recorded; otherwise a negative lldpctl_error_t value.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_get_connection
functions.description: Return the connection associated with a given atom. Each atom internally references its originating connection.
requirements: atom must be a valid atom obtained from the API.
Returned pointer is borrowed; do not free with lldpctl_release().

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_inc_ref
functions.description: Increment the reference count of an atom to take ownership or extend its lifetime.
requirements: atom must be a valid atom pointer (non-NULL).
Use balanced lldpctl_atom_dec_ref() to avoid leaks.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_dec_ref
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of an atom; when it reaches 0 the atom is freed immediately.
requirements: atom may be NULL (no operation).
After the count reaches 0, the atom is invalid; do not access it afterwards.

functions.name: lldpctl_watch_callback
functions.description: Deprecated: Register a callback to be invoked when neighbor changes are detected. Performs I/O to enable notifications and may return WOULDBLOCK. Once registered, the connection is dedicated to receiving notifications.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection handle.
cb must be a valid function implementing lldpctl_change_callback semantics.
May return LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK; caller should retry later if using non-blocking I/O.
After registering, do not use the connection for other operations; otherwise LLDPCTL_ERR_INVALID_STATE will occur.
Within the callback, the provided interface and neighbor atoms are stolen (their refs are decremented at the end); increment their ref in the callback if you need to keep them.
Within the callback, do not use the provided connection or call lldpctl_atom_set_* on interface/neighbor; doing so leads to LLDPCTL_ERR_INVALID_STATE.

functions.name: lldpctl_watch_callback2
functions.description: Register a callback (without the conn parameter) to be invoked when neighbor changes are detected. Performs I/O to enable notifications and may return WOULDBLOCK. After registration, the connection is reserved for notifications.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection handle.
cb must be a valid function implementing lldpctl_change_callback2 semantics.
May return LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK; caller should retry later if using non-blocking I/O.
After registering, do not use the connection for other operations; otherwise LLDPCTL_ERR_INVALID_STATE will occur.
Within the callback, the provided interface and neighbor atoms are stolen; increment their ref if you need to keep them.

functions.name: lldpctl_watch
functions.description: Block until the next change notification is received, then return. Intended as the main loop when using the built-in blocking I/O mechanism.
requirements: conn must be a valid synchronous-callback connection set up for notifications.
Returns 0 on success; a negative value indicates an error.

functions.name: lldpctl_watch_sync_unblock
functions.description: Unblock another thread currently blocked in lldpctl_watch() for the same synchronous-callback connection. This function is signal-safe.
requirements: conn must be the synchronous callback connection whose waiter you intend to unblock.
Has no effect if no thread is blocked in lldpctl_watch() for this conn.

functions.name: lldpctl_get_configuration
functions.description: Fetch the global configuration atom from the lldpd daemon. May perform I/O; with non-blocking I/O it may need to be retried if WOULDBLOCK is set.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection handle.
On NULL return, use lldpctl_last_error(conn) to distinguish errors; if LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later.
Returned atom is a new reference; caller must eventually lldpctl_atom_dec_ref() it.

functions.name: lldpctl_get_interfaces
functions.description: Fetch the list (iterable atom) of available interfaces/ports from lldpd. May perform I/O; with non-blocking I/O it may require retry.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection handle.
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(conn); if LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later.
The returned list is iterable via lldpctl_atom_iter(); caller must dec-ref the atom when done.

functions.name: lldpctl_get_local_chassis
functions.description: Fetch information related to the local chassis as an atom. May perform I/O and may require retry in non-blocking mode.
requirements: conn must be valid.
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(conn); if LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later.
Returned atom is a new reference; caller must dec-ref.

functions.name: lldpctl_get_port
functions.description: Fetch detailed information for a given interface/port atom (typically obtained from iterating lldpctl_get_interfaces()). May perform I/O and may require retry in non-blocking mode.
requirements: port must be an atom obtained from iterating the interfaces list returned by lldpctl_get_interfaces().
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(lldpctl_atom_get_connection(port)); if LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later.
Returned atom is a new reference; caller must dec-ref.

functions.name: lldpctl_get_default_port
functions.description: Fetch the default port settings atom used as a template for new ports. May perform I/O and may require retry in non-blocking mode.
requirements: conn must be valid.
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(conn); if LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later.
Returned atom is a new reference; caller must dec-ref.

functions.name: lldpctl_key_get_map
functions.description: Return a mapping table from integer values to strings for a given key (when such mapping exists). Useful to translate between numeric constants and human-readable names and to accept string values in setters.
requirements: key must be a valid lldpctl_key_t; returns NULL if no map is available.
Returned map is terminated with an entry whose value is 0.
The string names are suitable for use with set operations that accept strings.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_get
functions.description: Retrieve a piece of information from an atom as another atom (for complex/iterable values). Returns a new reference which the caller must release.
requirements: Only keys documented as atom-accessible (A/AL) can be retrieved this way; otherwise NULL is returned.
If atom is NULL, returns NULL and no error is raised (convenience).
Returned atom is not borrowed; caller must lldpctl_atom_dec_ref() when done.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_set
functions.description: Set a piece of information on an atom using another atom value. Returns the updated atom on success or NULL on error. Some sets commit immediately; others require writing the modified atom back to a parent atom.
requirements: Key must support being written with an atom (per lldpctl_key_t documentation).
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(atom->conn). If LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later with the exact same parameters. If LLDPCTL_ERR_BAD_VALUE, the provided value atom is not acceptable.
Do not assume the change is committed unless documented as immediate (WO); otherwise write the resulting atom back to the appropriate parent/container.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_get_str
functions.description: Retrieve a string representation for a key from an atom. For some keys this is a formatted string (e.g., MAC as "00:11:22:33:44:55").
requirements: Only keys documented as string-accessible (S/IS/BS) can be retrieved this way; otherwise NULL is returned.
If atom is NULL, returns NULL and no error is raised (convenience).
Returned C string may be owned by the atom; duplicate it if you need it after the atom’s lifetime.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_set_str
functions.description: Set a piece of information on an atom using a null-terminated string value. Returns the updated atom on success or NULL on error.
requirements: Key must support string write (W/WON as applicable). Some keys accept NULL to reset (marked (N)).
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(atom->conn). If LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later with the exact same parameters. If LLDPCTL_ERR_BAD_VALUE, the provided value is invalid.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_get_buffer
functions.description: Retrieve a binary buffer value for a key from an atom, returning a pointer and setting the length. The buffer may be internally owned by the atom.
requirements: Only keys documented as buffer-accessible (B/BS) can be retrieved this way; otherwise NULL is returned.
If atom is NULL, returns NULL and sets *length to 0; no error is raised (convenience).
Caller should not modify or free the returned buffer; duplicate it if needed beyond the atom’s lifetime.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_set_buffer
functions.signature: lldpctl_atom_t *lldpctl_atom_set_buffer(lldpctl_atom_t *atom, lldpctl_key_t key, const uint8_t *value, size_t length)
functions.description: Set a piece of information on an atom from a binary buffer. Returns the updated atom on success or NULL on error.
requirements: Key must support buffer write (W).

On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(atom->conn). If LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later with the exact same parameters. If LLDPCTL_ERR_BAD_VALUE, the provided value/length is invalid for the key.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_get_int
functions.description: Retrieve an integer value for a key from an atom. Returns -1 when the value is not available; only lldpctl_last_error() can disambiguate errors, though most values are non-negative.
requirements: Only keys documented as integer-accessible (I/IS) can be retrieved this way.
Caller should use lldpctl_last_error(lldpctl_atom_get_connection(atom)) to differentiate a legitimate negative value from an error when in doubt.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_set_int
functions.signature: lldpctl_atom_t *lldpctl_atom_set_int(lldpctl_atom_t *atom, lldpctl_key_t key, long int value)
functions.description: Set a piece of information on an atom using an integer value. Returns the updated atom on success or NULL on error.
requirements: Key must support integer write (W/WO as applicable).
On NULL return, check lldpctl_last_error(atom->conn). If LLDPCTL_ERR_WOULDBLOCK, retry later with the exact same parameters. If LLDPCTL_ERR_BAD_VALUE, the provided integer is invalid for the key.

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_iter
functions.description: Create an iterator over an iterable atom (lists such as interfaces, VLANs, neighbors). Returns NULL if the atom is empty or on error.
requirements: atom must be an iterable atom (AL).
If atom is NULL, returns NULL and no error is recorded (convenience).
The iterator is used with lldpctl_atom_iter_next() and lldpctl_atom_iter_value().

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_iter_next
functions.description: Advance an iterator to the next element of an iterable atom. Returns a new iterator position or NULL when no more elements.
requirements: atom must be the same iterable atom used to create the iterator.
iter must be a valid iterator for atom.
If atom is NULL, returns NULL and no error is recorded (convenience).

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_iter_value
functions.description: Return the atom corresponding to the current iterator position.
requirements: atom and iter must correspond to the same iterable sequence.
Returned atom follows normal reference counting rules described by the library (the foreach macro decrements it automatically).

functions.name: lldpctl_atom_create
functions.description: Create a new element suitable for appending to an iterable atom via lldpctl_atom_set(). The new object may need initialization via setters before being written back.
requirements: atom must be a container that supports creation (keys marked with (C) on their lists).
The newly created element should be appended by writing it to the list with lldpctl_atom_set(); deletion from lists is not available.
Avoid getters on a freshly created object until fully initialized, as internal buffers might not be set until the first set.

unharnessable_functions.name: lldpctl_watch_callback
unharnessable_functions.reason: Registering and driving the neighbor watch requires long-lived I/O and a valid lldpd daemon, and may block or require complex callback types not safely provided in this harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: lldpctl_watch_callback2
unharnessable_functions.reason: Neighbor watch registration dedicates the connection and performs blocking/non-blocking I/O with callbacks that are not safely modeled in this single-call harness.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path (for Unix-domain socket path). Must often be within
# system limits (e.g., ~108 bytes for sockaddr_un on many systems). We'll
# generate a variety of valid paths: absolute, relative, nested, with dot
# segments, tilde-expanded-looking (but we won't expand), and with typical
# socket filename suffixes. Keep total <= 4096 bytes and typical Unix limits.

MAX_TOTAL_LEN = 256  # keep conservative for sockaddr_un sun_path limits

ABS_DIRS = [
    "/var/run",
    "/run",
    "/tmp",
    "/var/tmp",
    "/dev/shm",
    "/usr/local/var/run",
]

REL_PREFIXES = [".", "..", "./var", "../run", "./tmp", "build", "out", "socketdir"]

SOCK_BASENAMES = [
    "lldpd.socket",
    "lldpd.sock",
    "lldpctl.sock",
    "control.sock",
    "ctl.sock",
    "daemon.sock",
    "sock",
    "s",
]

# Components that may appear in a path
COMPONENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_."


def _rand_name(r: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(COMPONENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _join_limit(parts: List[str], is_abs: bool, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Join ensuring we don't exceed max_len
    sep = "/"
    base = "/" if is_abs else ""
    path = base + sep.join(parts)
    if len(path) <= max_len:
        return path
    # Trim from the left (keep filename)
    filename = parts[-1] if parts else "sock"
    # Try to keep at least one dir
    for keep_dirs in range(len(parts) - 1, -1, -1):
        cand_parts = parts[:keep_dirs] + [filename]
        cand = base + sep.join(cand_parts)
        if len(cand) <= max_len:
            return cand
    # Fallback to filename only
    return ("/" if is_abs else "") + filename[: max(1, max_len - (1 if is_abs else 0))]


def _make_absolute_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(ABS_DIRS)
    depth = r.randint(0, 4)
    parts = [p for p in base.split("/") if p]
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_name(r))
    # choose a socket-like basename or random
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        basename = r.choice(SOCK_BASENAMES)
        # maybe prefix with lldpd-
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            basename = f"lldpd-{_rand_name(r,1,6)}-{basename}" if r.random() < 0.4 else f"{_rand_name(r,3,8)}-{basename}"
    else:
        basename = _rand_name(r) + (".sock" if r.random() < 0.7 else "")
    parts.append(basename)
    return _join_limit(parts, True, MAX_TOTAL_LEN)


def _make_relative_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = r.choice(REL_PREFIXES)
    parts = [p for p in prefix.split("/") if p]
    depth = r.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        # occasionally add dot segments
        roll = r.random()
        if roll < 0.2:
            parts.append(".")
        elif roll < 0.3:
            parts.append("..")
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_name(r))
    basename = r.choice(SOCK_BASENAMES) if r.random() < 0.8 else _rand_name(r) + (".sock" if r.random() < 0.6 else "")
    parts.append(basename)
    # Reinsert dot segments literally (no normalization)
    norm_parts: List[str] = []
    for p in parts:
        norm_parts.append(p)
    return _join_limit(norm_parts, False, MAX_TOTAL_LEN)


def _make_hidden_tmp_socket(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common pattern: /tmp/.X11-unix style hidden dir
    dir_name = "." + _rand_name(r, 3, 8)
    parts = ["tmp", dir_name, _rand_name(r, 2, 6) + ".sock"]
    return _join_limit(["tmp", dir_name, parts[-1]], True, MAX_TOTAL_LEN)


def _maybe_trailing_slash(path: str, r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Rarely add a trailing slash then a filename to keep valid
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        return (path.rstrip("/") + "/" + _rand_name(r, 1, 6))[:MAX_TOTAL_LEN]
    return path


def _ensure_valid(path: str) -> str:
    # Ensure not empty and not only '/'
    if not path:
        return "./sock"
    if path == "/":
        return "/tmp/sock"
    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose one of several styles with weighted probabilities
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.55:
        path = _make_absolute_path(r)
    elif choice < 0.85:
        path = _make_relative_path(r)
    else:
        path = _make_hidden_tmp_socket(r)

    # Occasionally add nested subdirs in front for more diversity (still valid)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        extra_depth = r.randint(1, 3)
        prefix = "/" if path.startswith("/") else ""
        parts = [p for p in path.split("/") if p]
        # Insert extra segments before basename
        if parts:
            head = parts[:-1]
            tail = parts[-1]
            for _ in range(extra_depth):
                head.append(_rand_name(r, 1, 6))
            path = _join_limit(head + [tail], prefix == "/", MAX_TOTAL_LEN)

    path = _maybe_trailing_slash(path, r)
    path = _ensure_valid(path)

    # Encode as UTF-8 bytes (ASCII subset used), return
    b = path.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    # Ensure <= 4096 bytes as required
    return b[:4096]

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate valid buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used by lldpctl_atom_set_str
# Data type: free-form, null-terminated string. We will generate diverse but valid C-strings
# (no embedded NUL, since FUZZ_PARAM_STR likely uses std::string). The fuzz stub may also pass
# NULL occasionally on its own; our job is to supply interesting non-NULL strings.
#
# Strategy:
# - Construct strings that resemble values commonly written via lldpctl_atom_set_str for various keys:
#   * Hostnames, interface patterns, management IPs, descriptions, TLV strings, OUI info, platform, etc.
# - Include edge cases: empty string, very long strings (<= 4096), unicode, whitespace, control chars (not NUL),
#   comma/semicolon separated lists, JSON-like, CID patterns, MAC-like, IP addresses (v4/v6), VLAN names.
# - Randomly choose one template and fill with randomized yet syntactically valid tokens to trigger different paths.
# - Return bytes without a terminating NUL; std::string will handle C-string conversion internally.

MAX_LEN = 4096

_letters = string.ascii_letters
_digits = string.digits
_hexd = string.hexdigits.lower()
_safe_punct = "-_.:+,/@[]()#= \t"  # avoid NUL


def _rand_hostname(r: random.Random) -> str:
    labels = []
    n = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(n):
        ln = r.randint(1, 10)
        s = r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)
        mid = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-') for _ in range(max(1, ln-1)))
        label = (s + mid).strip('-')
        labels.append(label or 'h')
    return '.'.join(labels)


def _rand_iface_pattern(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Patterns like eth*, enp3s0, bond[0-3], vlan+*, swp{1,2,3}
    choices = [
        lambda: f"eth{r.choice(['*', str(r.randint(0, 9))])}",
        lambda: f"enp{r.randint(0,9)}s{r.randint(0,9)}",
        lambda: f"bond[{r.randint(0,3)}-{r.randint(4,9)}]",
        lambda: f"vlan{r.randint(1,4094)}",
        lambda: f"swp{{{','.join(str(r.randint(1,48)) for _ in range(r.randint(1,4)))}}}",
        lambda: f"if*{r.randint(0,9)}",
    ]
    return choices[r.randrange(len(choices))]()


def _rand_ipv4(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return '.'.join(str(r.randint(0, 255)) for _ in range(4))


def _rand_ipv6(r: random.Random) -> str:
    groups = [format(r.getrandbits(16), 'x') for _ in range(8)]
    # Optionally compress
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        idx = r.randint(0, 6)
        groups[idx:idx+2] = ['']
        s = ':'.join(groups)
        s = s.replace(':::', '::')
        if not s.startswith('::') and r.random() < 0.5:
            s = s.replace('::', '::', 1)
        return s if '::' in s else ':'.join(groups)
    return ':'.join(groups)


def _rand_mac(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return ':'.join(f"{r.randint(0,255):02x}" for _ in range(6))


def _rand_oui_info(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # OUI subtype/info often arbitrary ASCII; prefer visible range including commas
    ln = r.randint(4, 64)
    return ''.join(r.choice(_letters + _digits + _safe_punct) for _ in range(ln)).strip()


def _rand_description(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = [
        f"Platform={r.choice(['Linux','BSD','ESXi','NX-OS','EOS'])}",
        f"Host={_rand_hostname(r)}",
        f"Iface={_rand_iface_pattern(r)}",
        f"MAC={_rand_mac(r)}",
        f"Mgmt={r.choice([_rand_ipv4(r), _rand_ipv6(r)])}",
    ]
    return '; '.join(parts)


def _rand_civic_address(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # key=value list for MED civic address
    keys = ["country", "A1", "A3", "A6", "HNO", "HNS", "LMK", "LOC"]
    kv = []
    for k in keys:
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            vlen = r.randint(1, 12)
            v = ''.join(r.choice(_letters + _digits + ' -') for _ in range(vlen)).strip()
            kv.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return ';'.join(kv)


def _rand_unicode_text(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some BMP unicode that stays in UTF-8 safely
    blocks = [
        (0x00A0, 0x00FF),  # Latin-1 supplement
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
        (0x0100, 0x017F),  # Latin Extended-A
    ]
    ln = r.randint(1, 128)
    out = []
    for _ in range(ln):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            out.append(r.choice(_letters + _digits + _safe_punct))
        else:
            b = r.choice(blocks)
            out.append(chr(r.randint(b[0], b[1])))
    return ''.join(out)


def _rand_keyval_list(r: random.Random) -> str:
    keys = ["tx-interval", "hostname", "platform", "description", "vlan-name", "oui-subtype"]
    vals = [
        str(r.randint(1, 120)),
        _rand_hostname(r),
        r.choice(["GenericOS", "lldpd", "SwitchOS", "RouterOS"]),
        _rand_description(r),
        f"VLAN{r.randint(1,4094)}",
        str(r.randint(0,255)),
    ]
    pairs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        k = r.choice(keys)
        v = r.choice(vals)
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return ','.join(pairs)


def _rand_json_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Not strict JSON but plausible config blob
    obj = {
        "hostname": _rand_hostname(r),
        "iface_pattern": _rand_iface_pattern(r),
        "mgmt": r.choice([_rand_ipv4(r), _rand_ipv6(r)]),
        "caps": [r.choice(["bridge","router","wlan","station"]) for _ in range(r.randint(1,3))],
    }
    caps = ','.join(f'"{c}"' for c in obj["caps"])
    return f'{{"hostname":"{obj["hostname"]}","iface":"{obj["iface_pattern"]}","mgmt":"{obj["mgmt"]}","caps":[{caps}]}}'


def _rand_controlish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include tabs, newlines, carriage returns, but avoid NUL
    ln = r.randint(1, 64)
    choices = _letters + _digits + _safe_punct + "\n\r\t"
    s = ''.join(r.choice(choices) for _ in range(ln))
    # Ensure it does not end with a backslash (can confuse some parsers)
    return s.rstrip('\\')


def _edge_cases(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",  # empty string
        " ",  # single space
        "\t\t",  # tabs
        _rand_ipv4(r),
        _rand_ipv6(r),
        _rand_mac(r),
        _rand_hostname(r),
        _rand_iface_pattern(r),
        "*",  # wildcard
        ",,,",  # separators only
    ]


def _build_pool(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool = []
    pool.append(_rand_description(r))
    pool.append(_rand_keyval_list(r))
    pool.append(_rand_civic_address(r))
    pool.append(_rand_json_like(r))
    pool.append(_rand_unicode_text(r))
    pool.append(_rand_controlish(r))
    pool.extend(_edge_cases(r))
    # Also include a long but valid ASCII block for stress
    long_len = r.randint(256, min(2048, MAX_LEN-1))
    long_block = ''.join(r.choice(_letters + _digits + _safe_punct) for _ in range(long_len))
    pool.append(long_block.rstrip('\x00'))
    return [s[:MAX_LEN-1] for s in pool]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _build_pool(r)
    choice = r.choice(pool)
    # Small chance to concatenate multiple valid forms to exercise parsers accepting lists
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        extra = r.choice(pool)
        sep = r.choice([",", ";", " ", "\n"])  # no NUL
        combined = (choice + sep + extra)[:MAX_LEN-1]
        return combined.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    return choice.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
